text:
**Subject: You'd be great at this (hear me out)**

Hi Sam,

The Riverside Community Library is looking for guest speakers for its Local Voices evening on November 14th, and I immediately thought of you. Before you say no, give me two minutes.

**Why you?** You know more about urban gardening than anyone I've met. The way you explained composting to me last spring finally made it click. People don't want a polished performer. They want someone who knows their stuff and cares about it. That's you.

**"But I hate public speaking."** I know. But this isn't a TED stage. It's a 10-minute talk to about 30 friendly neighbors in a library meeting room. Many introverts are excellent speakers because they prepare carefully and speak with substance instead of filler.

**"What if I freeze?"** You can use notes or slides, and there's a Q&A format option where the host guides the conversation. I'll also help you rehearse as many times as you want, and I'll be in the front row.

**"What's in it for me?"** You'll connect with people who share your passion without small talk, since they'll come to *you*. It's also a low-stakes way to build a skill that's useful at work. And honestly, you might enjoy it more than you expect.

**The ask:** Just let me send your name to the organizer. You can back out up to a week before if it really doesn't feel right. No pressure, no judgment.

You have something worth sharing. I'd love to see you share it.

Talk soon,
Alex

P.S. Coffee's on me after. Win-win.
